messages:
sanjay: Heads up — EU ingest spike landed yesterday, ~6M events tagged late. We need to recompute daily aggregates for the last 3 days. Thinking through options: slot a backfill job in low-traffic windows vs route to degraded but cheaper compute. Thoughts?

rachel: Oof. Do we know if events are duplicates or just late arrivals? duplicates mean idempotent upserts, simpler. late-only means re-run windowed aggregates.

sanjay: Early analysis says mostly late-only (source delay), few dup keys. So recompute needed to avoid undercounts in Dashboards.

omar: We should avoid creating a big concurrency spike during EU peak — suggested approach: schedule multiple small backfill slots across nights and use our routing policy to prefer spare dedicated nodes.

kevin: I worry about quota impacts — backfills consume tenant quotas (ingest tokens). If we schedule spiky backfills it will throttle production dashboards. Can we mark backfill jobs with a special "system_backfill" route that bypasses per-tenant quotas but runs on dedicated pool?

elaine: That requires infra changes to routing policy. Currently routing decisions are per-request: {region, tier, model_variant}. We'd need a new axis 'task_type' that influences pool selection. Not huge but needs review.

sanjay: Minimal infra change option: use existing routing by setting origin region to a low-cost EU pool that is dedicated and increase its capacity temporarily. No quota bypass but isolates tenant impact.

omar: Implementation sketch: break the 6M into 6 jobs of ~1M each, run nightly between 02:00-06:00 UTC, stagger starts, and set request-level header X-Backfill: true so we can track cost/metrics.

kevin: Agree on X-Backfill header for tracking. But we still need safe throttles. Suggest adding a controller that ensures global backfill concurrency <= 4 and per-tenant backfill concurrency <= 1.

elaine: If we add controller throttles, we can keep routing unchanged. Controller can check active jobs and gate start. We'll need a simple state table and leader election for HA.

rachel: Also need UX: Console should show a "Backfill jobs" card under Telemetry -> Recomputes with status and estimated finish. Product would like to surface cost estimate before start.

sanjay: I'll put together a short RFC: two-phase plan: (A) short-term: slotted nightly jobs + X-Backfill header + controller throttles; (B) mid-term: extend routing policy to include task_type and optional quota bypass for infra-initiated backfills.

kevin: +1. For short-term, can we use existing backfill runner? Example command we can reuse: ```
# run replay for day
./tools/backfill-runner --start 2026-03-15 --end 2026-03-15 --concurrency 2 --tag backfill_eu_march
```

backfill-bot: Scheduled backfill-runner job created: job_id=bf-20260318-01, window=2026-03-13..2026-03-15, concurrency=2, owner=sanjay. Logs: https://logs.internal/jobs/bf-20260318-01

omar: Perfect. I'll own the controller prototype and staging test. Sanjay — can you own the RFC + console mockups?

sanjay: Yep, will draft RFC today and link mocks. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: One last note — tag all compute with billing_label=backfill_eu_march so cost can be reconciled against the incident credit line.

sanjay: Added to RFC checklist.
__notes: single-thread Slack export style: messages in chronological order, senders prefixed by name. No title field included per agents.md.
